questions.question: How do you check your blind spots?

options.text: Look in your side mirrors.
Turn your head and look over your shoulders.
Look in your rearview mirror.
Stare straight ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head and look over your shoulders.
questions.explanation: Blind spots are areas around your vehicle that mirrors cannot show. Turn your head and look over your shoulders to check them.

questions.question: When exiting a highway, when should you slow down?

options.text: On the main road, just before the exit lane.
Once you see a toll booth.
Once you have moved into the exit lane.
When you first see the exit sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Once you have moved into the exit lane.
questions.explanation: Move into the exit lane first. Then slow down. Do not slow down before you enter the exit lane.

questions.question: What is the "No zone"?

options.text: A term used to describe blind spots around a truck or bus.
A special speed zone.
A roadway with restrictions on vehicle stereo volume.
The television show that replaced The Twilight Zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: A term used to describe blind spots around a truck or bus.
questions.explanation: Trucks and buses have blind spots on all sides, in the rear, and in the front. Cars cannot be seen in these areas. These blind spots are called the "No zone."

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Your current roadway ends ahead.
You must bear either right or left.
A four-way intersection is ahead.
A road joins from the right.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must bear either right or left.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a Y intersection is ahead. You must turn either right or left.

questions.question: When driving in traffic, what is safest?

options.text: Change your speed to stay alert.
Drive faster than the flow of traffic.
Drive slower than the flow of traffic.
Drive with the flow of traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive with the flow of traffic.
questions.explanation: Crashes happen when drivers go faster or slower than other vehicles. Always drive with the flow of traffic, within the posted speed limit.

questions.question: When entering a street from a driveway, you must:

options.text: Drive slowly to give approaching vehicles and pedestrians time to move.
Honk your horn so vehicles and pedestrians know to give you room.
Stop and proceed only when no pedestrians or vehicles are approaching.
You can ignore pedestrians if there is no sidewalk.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and proceed only when no pedestrians or vehicles are approaching.
questions.explanation: Always stop before entering the street from a driveway. Yield to any vehicles or pedestrians. Stop before crossing the sidewalk. Not stopping is illegal.

questions.question: When you see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights, you must:

options.text: Slow down and stay in your lane.
Keep driving in your lane.
Pull to the right curb and stop.
Stop exactly where you are.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the right curb and stop.
questions.explanation: When you see flashing lights or hear a siren on an emergency vehicle, pull over to the right curb or side of the road and stop immediately.

questions.question: You are waiting in the intersection to turn left. What should you do?

options.text: Signal and turn your wheels to the left.
Signal and keep your wheels straight.
Flash your headlights so drivers will let you through.
Drive around the rear of a car if it blocks you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal and keep your wheels straight.
questions.explanation: Always signal before turning. Keep your wheels straight while waiting to turn left. If a car hits you from behind, you will not be pushed into oncoming traffic.

questions.question: What does a red circle with a slash through it mean on a sign?

options.text: Drivers must come to a complete stop.
An action is forbidden.
Some drivers must yield to other drivers.
Drivers must drive under the speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: An action is forbidden.
questions.explanation: A red circle and slash on a sign means that action is forbidden. These signs are white with red and black markings.

questions.question: Where is it best to keep a space cushion around your vehicle?

options.text: Only in back of your vehicle.
Only on the left and right sides of your vehicle.
Only in front of your vehicle.
On all sides of the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: On all sides of the vehicle.
questions.explanation: Keep a cushion of space on all sides of your vehicle. This gives you time to react to hazards. Do not drive too close to vehicles on your left and right.

questions.question: ____ greatly increase stopping distances and crash severity.

options.text: High speeds
Slow speeds
Night drives
Uphill inclines

questions.correctAnswerText: High speeds
questions.explanation: High speeds greatly increase stopping distances and crash severity. The faster you drive, the harder your vehicle hits in a crash.

questions.question: You see a stopped emergency vehicle with flashing lights. You must:

options.text: Slow down. If possible, change lanes away from the stopped emergency vehicle.
Drive to the right side of the road and stop.
Stay in your lane and continue at the same speed.
Speed up to pass the stopped vehicle quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down. If possible, change lanes away from the stopped emergency vehicle.
questions.explanation: When you see a stopped emergency vehicle with flashing lights, you must change lanes to give it extra space. If you cannot change lanes safely, slow down below the speed limit. Always slow down and be ready to stop at emergency scenes.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: All traffic must turn left.
No left turn.
No U-turn.
Truck route to the left.

questions.correctAnswerText: No left turn.
questions.explanation: This sign means left turns are not allowed.

questions.question: You are on the interstate and pass your exit. You should:

options.text: Quickly cut across traffic to make your turn.
Make a U-turn to go back to the exit.
Continue driving and use the next exit.
Put your vehicle in reverse to go back to the exit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Continue driving and use the next exit.
questions.explanation: If you miss your exit, do not make a sudden turn. Continue to the next exit instead.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No turns are allowed on this road.
The road narrows ahead.
There are a series of curves ahead.
The road may be slippery when wet.

questions.correctAnswerText: There are a series of curves ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that the road ahead has three or more curves.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Yield.
Crossroad ahead.
Keep right.
Yield ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield.
questions.explanation: This three-sided sign warns you to slow down at an intersection. Be ready to stop for other traffic or pedestrians. You can proceed when it is safe.

questions.question: A flashing red traffic light works the same way as:

options.text: A slow sign.
A yield sign.
A stop sign.
An intersection sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: A stop sign.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means you must stop and let all other traffic pass before proceeding.

questions.question: An emergency vehicle is approaching with flashing red or blue lights. You should:

options.text: Try to reach your destination before the emergency vehicle catches up.
Keep driving but stay out of its way.
Pull over to the side of the road and stop completely.
Stop in the middle of an intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over to the side of the road and stop completely.
questions.explanation: You must yield to all emergency vehicles using sirens or flashing lights. Pull over to the right edge of the road when possible. If you are in an intersection, drive through first, then pull over.

questions.question: To enter a freeway:

options.text: Signal, yield to traffic, and enter at the same speed traffic is moving.
Signal and enter. Freeway traffic must yield to you.
Drive slowly so you can check traffic.
Always come to a complete stop first.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, yield to traffic, and enter at the same speed traffic is moving.
questions.explanation: When entering a freeway, signal and merge at the same speed as other traffic. Always yield to vehicles already on the freeway.

questions.question: The best way to handle a tailgater is to:

options.text: Speed up to increase the distance between you.
Brake hard to make them back off.
Change lanes or slow down gradually to let them pass.
Ignore them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes or slow down gradually to let them pass.
questions.explanation: Watch traffic behind you regularly. If someone is tailgating, slow down gradually to let them pass. Most rear-end crashes happen when drivers follow too closely.

questions.question: If you miss your exit on the freeway, what should you do?

options.text: Go to the next exit.
Make a U-turn through the median.
Pull onto the shoulder and back up to the exit.
Flag down a police officer to escort you back to your exit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Go to the next exit.
questions.explanation: If you miss your exit, take the next exit. Do not stop, back up, swerve across lanes, or cross the median. These actions are illegal and dangerous.

questions.question: When backing up, what should you do?

options.text: Use only your mirrors.
Flash your lights.
Open your door to see if it is safe.
Turn your head and look through the rear window.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head and look through the rear window.
questions.explanation: Always check behind your vehicle before backing up. Children and small objects are hard to see from the driver's seat. Turn your head to look through the rear window while backing. Do not rely only on mirrors or sensors.

questions.question: Your tire blows out while driving. What should you do?

options.text: Slam on your brakes.
Hold the steering wheel tightly and slow to a stop.
Keep driving normally.
Turn on emergency flashers and continue driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the steering wheel tightly and slow to a stop.
questions.explanation: Do not brake immediately. Grip the steering wheel firmly and stay in your lane. Reduce speed gradually by releasing the accelerator. Once moving very slowly, apply brakes lightly and pull off the road safely.

questions.question: When can you drive around the gates at a railroad crossing?

options.text: When the train has passed.
Never.
When the lights have stopped flashing.
When other drivers drive around the gates.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never.
questions.explanation: You must stop at all railroad crossings when signals warn of a train. These signals include flashing red lights, lowered gates, a flagger, or train whistles. Never go around a lowered gate.

questions.question: What does a flashing red traffic light mean?

options.text: It means the same thing as a stop sign.
The traffic signal is broken.
You do not have to stop completely.
Driving conditions are dangerous.

questions.correctAnswerText: It means the same thing as a stop sign.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means the same as a stop sign. Come to a complete stop, yield to traffic and pedestrians, and only proceed when it is safe.

questions.question: What lights should you use when driving in rain?

options.text: Low beam headlights.
High beam headlights.
Parking lights.
No lights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights when driving in rain.

questions.question: What should you do if a car is tailgating you?

options.text: Move to the right lane if it is open.
If no right lane is open, wait until ahead is clear and reduce your speed slowly to let them pass.
Never brake suddenly.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: If being tailgated and a right lane is open, move right. If no right lane exists, wait until the road ahead is clear and reduce speed slowly to encourage them to pass. Never brake suddenly, as this increases the risk of being hit.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Entrance to full parking lots.
Entrance to road construction areas.
Entrance to dead-end streets.
Do not enter from this direction on one-way streets and expressway ramps.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not enter from this direction on one-way streets and expressway ramps.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that a road is one-way and you must not enter from your current direction.

questions.question: You are turning left at a busy intersection and cannot see all lanes. What should you do?

options.text: Speed up as soon as the first lane clears.
Wait until you can see all lanes are clear before turning.
Wait for another driver to wave you across.
Move into each lane of traffic as it clears.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until you can see all lanes are clear before turning.
questions.explanation: Never start a left turn until you can see that all lanes you need to cross are clear and the turn is safe.

questions.question: You are angry after a bad day at work. What should you do before driving home?

options.text: Play the radio loudly to distract yourself.
Drive fast on the interstate to release your anger.
Take a few minutes to calm down before you start driving.
Stop at a bar for a few drinks before driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take a few minutes to calm down before you start driving.
questions.explanation: Take time to cool off before driving when upset or angry. Letting emotions affect your driving is poor judgment and dangerous to yourself and others.
